candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata (Register of payment institutions and their agents)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative population list of every licensed payment institution in Montenegro, with per-entity registration PDFs (reg_*.pdf) naming permitted payment services, agents and branches. This is the master actor map for the payments cell and the entry point for snowballing to company sites, tariffs and licence changes. Observed entries: Montenegro Transfers, Capital Transfer MNE, Moneta MNE, Payspot ME, Alta Pay Group, Prestopay, Business Integration and Business Intelligence d.o.o.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled HTML fetch + diff of the entity list; download each linked reg_*.pdf and diff versions to detect licence scope changes, new agents, and new entrants.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on regulator register terminology
queries_used: platna institucija Crna Gora licenca izdavalac elektronskog novca registar CBCG

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata (E-money institutions register)
candidates.why_relevant: Official e-money issuer register. At time of scouting the page stated no e-money institution is currently entered ('U Registru trenutno nema upisane institucije za elektronski novac') — that emptiness is itself a market-structure signal, and the page is the tripwire for the first ME EMI licence.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency (monthly) HTML diff; alert on any transition from the empty-register notice to a listed entity.
candidates.discovered_via_method: regulator site navigation from register index
queries_used: platna institucija Crna Gora licenca izdavalac elektronskog novca registar CBCG

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Spisak platnih institucija i institucija za elektronski novac kojima je oduzeto odobrenje (withdrawn authorisations)
candidates.why_relevant: Negative-licensing list: exits, revocations and enforcement outcomes for PSPs/EMIs. Pairs with the positive register to give full churn of the payments population.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly HTML/PDF diff, joined on entity name with the active register.
queries_used: platna institucija Crna Gora licenca izdavalac elektronskog novca registar CBCG

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registri (payment-area register index)
candidates.why_relevant: Index of all payment-domain registers (payment systems, payment institutions, e-money institutions, withdrawn authorisations). Single hub to detect newly created register types as PSD2-style regulation is implemented.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl seed; monitor link set for new register pages.
queries_used: platna institucija Crna Gora licenca izdavalac elektronskog novca registar CBCG

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Pregledi tarifa pružalaca platnih usluga (payment service provider tariff overviews)
candidates.why_relevant: Regulator-mandated, centrally aggregated tariff/fee publications for payment service providers (bank tariffs plus CBCG's own and other PSPs). Directly delivers the pricing/tariff dimension of the cell — card acceptance fees, transfer fees, account fees — in comparable form across providers.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate per-provider subpages (e.g. /tarife-banaka/nlb-banka-ad-podgorica), download tariff PDFs on a quarterly cadence, extract fee tables and diff over time. Note the parent path without /tarife-banaka returned 404 on one attempt — treat the parent as unverified, not dead.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on tariff terminology + snowball
queries_used: cbcg.me "pregledi tarifa pružalaca platnih usluga" tarife banaka platnih institucija
naknade za platne usluge Crna Gora objava

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Podaci o platnim uslugama i elektronskom novcu (payment services & e-money statistics)
candidates.why_relevant: Quarterly regulatory reporting aggregates on payment services and e-money submitted by PSPs under the CBCG reporting decision — card, POS, ATM and transfer volumes/values. The quantitative backbone against which individual actor announcements can be sanity-checked.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly XLS/PDF harvest of the statistics archive (series observed back to ~2006); parse into a time series of card/POS/ATM counts and values.
queries_used: CBCG statistika platnih kartica POS ATM broj transakcija izvještaj platni promet

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Platni promet i platni sistemi (secondary legislation / podzakonski akti)
candidates.why_relevant: The decisions and rulebooks that define what payment institutions and e-money issuers must publish (tariff disclosure, reporting decisions, licensing conditions). Determines the existence and format of every other disclosure source in this cell, and signals PSD2/SEPA alignment steps.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Watch page for new/amended 'odluka' PDFs; diff titles and dates.
queries_used: platna institucija Crna Gora licenca izdavalac elektronskog novca registar CBCG

candidates.source_name: CBCG FinTech Hub (fintechhub.cbcg.me)
candidates.why_relevant: Regulator's dedicated fintech portal: strategy, fintech surveys and ecosystem mapping. Names non-bank payment players and emerging PSP/e-money aspirants that never appear in the licence register, and flags regulatory-sandbox style initiatives.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl; extract company names from ecosystem/survey publications to expand the actor map.
queries_used: Crna Gora fintech "platne usluge" novi procesor kartica saopštenje 2025 acquiring e-commerce

candidates.source_name: CRPS — Centralni registar privrednih subjekata (Montenegro company register, Tax Administration)
candidates.why_relevant: Company-level registry for every ME-incorporated payment institution, processor and acquirer: legal form, ownership, beneficial owners (register established Aug 2021), statutory changes and filings. The only route to ownership/control and capital changes for privately held PSPs that publish nothing themselves.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Targeted lookups by entity name for the seven registered PIs; periodic re-query to catch capital/ownership/status changes. Form-driven — needs a session-aware fetcher, not a plain crawler.
queries_used: Crna Gora CRPS Poreska uprava registar privrednih subjekata finansijski izvještaji objava

candidates.source_name: Payten (Asseco SEE card-business spin-off) — regional processor site
candidates.why_relevant: Dominant SEE card processor / ATM-POS services vendor (self-reported ~600k POS, 9,500+ ATMs, 15m+ card transactions monthly across 16 countries), spun out of Asseco SEE in 2017 and owner of Monri since 2019. Its news and country pages reveal processing, acquiring-as-a-service and merchant wins that touch Montenegrin banks and merchants.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor news/press section and any ME-specific country page; filter items mentioning Crna Gora/Montenegro or ME bank names. Cross-read with Asseco SEE investor reporting for segment numbers.
candidates.discovered_via_method: vendor-side reasoning (who sells processing into ME) + local-language search
queries_used: Payten OR "Asseco SEE" Crna Gora kartično poslovanje procesiranje POS

candidates.source_name: CKB (Crnogorska komercijalna banka / OTP) — acquiring & POS pages
candidates.why_relevant: Largest ME acquirer by its own claim (POS network since 2002, stated 4,000+ terminals). Bank-acquirer pages carry merchant-service conditions, terminal counts and card-scheme partnerships — the acquiring half of this cell is mostly bank-owned in ME, so bank acquiring pages are the substitute for standalone acquirer disclosures.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly diff of POS/acquiring/e-commerce pages and merchant fee documents; log stated terminal counts as a time series.

candidates.why_relevant: Active ME internet-acquiring provider for merchants; the page documents e-commerce gateway partners, supported schemes and onboarding conditions. Key signal for which processing/gateway stack is used for card-not-present in Montenegro.

candidates.why_relevant: Official EU-side communication on Montenegro becoming operationally part of SEPA — a structural change that resets cross-border euro payment pricing and opens the market to EU-licensed PSPs. Anchors the timeline for rail changes affecting every actor in this cell.

candidates.why_relevant: Describes the operation of the national payment system(s) and publishes system-level statistics. Establishes which rails PSPs can reach, participant lists, and settlement volumes — necessary context for interpreting any processor/acquirer claim.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Serbian/Montenegrin for a domestically licensed card processor or standalone acquirer ('kartično poslovanje', 'procesiranje kartica', 'Multicard', 'Digital Systems') and found no Montenegro-domiciled dedicated card-processing company with its own disclosure surface.
negative_findings.result_summary: Card processing in ME appears to be delivered by banks (notably CKB/OTP, Hipotekarna) and by regional vendors (Payten/Asseco SEE, Monri) rather than by a locally licensed standalone processor. Searches returned only unrelated hardware retailers for 'procesori'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's 'card processors and acquirers' half must be tracked indirectly through bank acquiring pages and regional vendor announcements; expecting local processor disclosures would leave a permanent blind spot.

negative_findings.description: The CBCG e-money institution register page states that no e-money institution is currently entered.
negative_findings.result_summary: 'U Registru trenutno nema upisane institucije za elektronski novac' observed on the register page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: There is currently no ME-licensed EMI population to monitor; e-money activity, if any, arrives via banks or EU-passported entities. The register should be treated as a tripwire rather than a data feed.

negative_findings.description: Searched for press releases / 'saopštenja' from the licensed ME payment institutions (Payspot ME, Alta Pay Group, Moneta MNE, Prestopay, Capital Transfer MNE, Business Integration and Business Intelligence).
negative_findings.result_summary: No dedicated press-release or investor-relations sections were located for these entities; several (Prestopay, Business Integration and Business Intelligence, Moneta MNE) returned no identifiable corporate website at all. Capital Transfer MNE's only visible channel is social media.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Corporate-disclosure coverage for ME payment institutions cannot rely on IR pages; it must lean on the CBCG register PDFs, CRPS filings and local news pickup.

negative_findings.description: A fetch of the tariff-overview parent path returned HTTP 404 while its child path /tarife-banaka appears in search results and in-site navigation.
negative_findings.result_summary: https://www.cbcg.me/me/kljucne-funkcije/platni-promet/pregledi-tarifa-pruzalaca-platnih-usluga returned 404 on a single attempt; the section is very likely live under language-prefixed or child paths (me/, eng/, r/, legal/ variants observed).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Recorded as unverified rather than dead, per the rule that one failed fetch is a hypothesis. The verification pass should probe the language-prefix variants before marking anything broken.

negative_findings.description: Searched for annual reports / earnings disclosures by ME payment institutions and e-money issuers.
negative_findings.result_summary: None of the seven registered payment institutions is listed on the Montenegro Stock Exchange or publishes annual reports publicly; financial statements are reachable only via CRPS/Tax Administration filings.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The run topics 'annual reports', 'investor relations' and 'earnings' have essentially no direct surface in this cell; CRPS becomes the mandatory substitute and should be prioritised in collection design.

coverage_gaps.description: Three registered payment institutions (Prestopay d.o.o., Business Integration and Business Intelligence d.o.o., and to a lesser extent Moneta MNE) have no located web presence; only their CBCG register PDFs describe them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch and parse the individual register PDFs (reg_prestopay.pdf, reg_busin_integr_and_busin_intell.pdf, reg_moneta.pdf) and run CRPS lookups to establish ownership, services and any trading names that would make them findable.

coverage_gaps.description: No interchange-fee / merchant-service-charge disclosure source identified for Montenegro (no equivalent of an EU IFR interchange publication was found).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search CBCG regulation pages and card-scheme (Visa/Mastercard) country interchange documents for Montenegro; also check whether ME acquirers publish MSC ranges in their tariff PDFs on the CBCG tariff pages.

coverage_gaps.description: Montenegrin-Cyrillic and alternative transliteration variants (e.g. 'платна институција', 'електронски новац') were not exercised in this pass; all local-language searching used Latin script.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run key seed queries in Cyrillic and with alias spellings (e-novac, elektronski novac, PSP, PI, IEN) to catch documents indexed only in Cyrillic.

coverage_gaps.description: Public-procurement and tender sources were not scouted, though bank/state tenders for POS, ATM and processing services are a strong indirect reveal of processor market share and contract renewals.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the ME public procurement portal (CEJN / portal javnih nabavki, gov.me) as a scouted source in the next pass, with queries for POS terminali, procesiranje kartica, platni promet usluge.

coverage_gaps.description: EU/EEA passported PSPs and e-money issuers serving Montenegrin customers cross-border (post-SEPA) are not covered by any ME register identified here.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Cross-reference EBA and neighbouring-jurisdiction registers, plus CBCG statements on cross-border provision, to see whether foreign-licensed EMIs are recognised or notified in ME.

brief: Montenegro's payments population is small, regulator-centric and almost entirely non-disclosing: the Central Bank of Montenegro is the single indispensable source, holding the payment-institution register (seven licensed entities, each with a downloadable registration PDF), the currently empty e-money register, the withdrawn-authorisation list, PSP tariff overviews and quarterly payment-services/e-money statistics. Almost no ME payment institution publishes press releases, annual reports or investor material, so corporate-disclosure coverage must be reconstructed from CBCG register PDFs, CRPS company filings, and the handful of actor sites that do exist (Payspot ME, Montenegro Transfers/Alta group, Capital Transfer MNE via social channels only). The acquiring and card-processing half of the cell has no domestic standalone processor: it is visible through bank acquiring pages (CKB claims the largest POS network, Hipotekarna for e-commerce) and through regional vendor announcements from Payten/Asseco SEE and Monri. Structural change is coming from policy rather than from the actors — SEPA operational membership and PSD2-style alignment — which the CBCG FinTech Hub, EU delegation communications and local wires (MINA Business, Borba) surface earliest.
